text: The Lyceum, finished in 1848, is the oldest building on campus.
The name "Ole Miss" came from a student contest to name the 1897 yearbook.
William Faulkner lived at Rowan Oak, his home in Oxford, from 1930 until his death in 1962.
Faulkner won the Nobel Prize in Literature for 1949.
In 1962, James Meredith became the first Black student to enroll at Ole Miss.
Vaught-Hemingway Stadium is named for coach John Vaught and Judge William Hemingway.
Oxford's Double Decker Arts Festival is named for the red double-decker bus the town brought over from England.
Thacker Mountain Radio, a live music and books radio show, is recorded in Oxford.
Square Books opened on the Oxford Square in 1979.
